source: Internet Archive djen-tjro-2025 OCR cadernos (public DJEN publications) for the original 20-doc seed; TJRO JURIS system (src/tjro_juris, real digitally-native court text, not OCR) for the 20-doc expansion batch, the 20-doc preliminar-targeted Round A batch, the 20-doc costs/fees-targeted Round B batch, the 18-doc general-volume Round C batch, the 8-doc honorarios_fim-targeted Round D batch, the 25-doc model-assisted-correction Round E batch (2017-07-ACORDAO.parquet), and the 20-doc Gemini-annotated Round F batch (2023-09-SENTENCA.parquet, via Internet Archive item tjro-juris-2023)
per_class_note: Counts above are train-split only, matching the original convention. Round D closed the last G2 gap: honorarios_fim went from 6 to 12 in train (>=10 minimum). Round E (25 docs, see notes) added structural-category volume across the board (e.g. acordao_decisorio_fim 21->37, cabecalho_inicio 69->92, voto_inicio 22->40) by deliberately excluding ref_normativa from its own labeling effort -- ref_normativa was already the single most abundant category (824 examples pre-Round-E, already far past any minimum) so Round E's per-document labeling budget was spent entirely on the structural anchors an audited-precision pass on this same checkpoint had just shown to be the model's weakest categories (resultado/cabecalho/voto/relatorio/acordao_decisorio pairs). Round E's ref_normativa count (931) comes only from spans the correcting subagents happened to keep/fix from the model's own predictions, not from fresh labeling. Round F (20 sentenca docs, see notes) was pure-volume, LLM-labeled rather than subagent-labeled, and closed the G5 volume gate (131->151 total docs, >=150 minimum): it lifted fundamentacao_legal 31->57 and dispositivo_abertura 47->62 the most, since sentencas structurally carry both far more densely than the acordao-heavy prior rounds. ALL G1, G2, and G5 gates are now clear across every split; only G4 (waived, multi-tribunal) remains.
labeler: prompt_subagents:haiku (original 20-doc seed, one labeling subagent per batch, acordaos first); prompt_subagents:general-purpose, one per document, for the 20-doc JURIS expansion batch, the 20-doc Round A preliminar-targeted batch, the 20-doc Round B costs/fees-targeted batch, the 18-doc Round C general-volume batch, the 8-doc Round D honorarios_fim-targeted batch, and the 25-doc Round E model-assisted-correction batch; llm_annotator:gemini-2.5-flash + gemini-2.5-flash-lite (via litellm, regex-anchored span extraction resolved locally to character offsets, per scripts/annotate_with_llm.py's approach) for the 20-doc Round F batch
verification_note: IMPORTANT provenance distinction: the original 20-doc seed's val+test went through a decorrelated 4-role Sonnet ensemble verification pass before being trusted as eval-quality gold. The 20-doc JURIS expansion batch, the 20-doc Round A preliminar-targeted batch (tjro_juris_acordao_prelim_*), the 20-doc Round B costs/fees-targeted batch (tjro_juris_sentenca_costs_*), the 18-doc Round C general-volume batch (tjro_juris_sentenca_vol_*), the 8-doc Round D batch (tjro_juris_sentenca_hon_*), the 25-doc Round E model-assisted-correction batch, and the 20-doc Round F batch have NOT gone through that ensemble verification -- each has single-subagent labeling (one general-purpose agent per document, each independently briefed with the full annotation guideline), mechanical validation (opf_annotate.py validate: 0 offset/overlap/label-space errors across all splits), and a manual spot-check of a sample of records by the orchestrating session (not exhaustive, not the full ensemble). Round E additionally started from a trained checkpoint's own predictions plus an independent 25-subagent audit of those predictions (correct/wrong_category/wrong_boundary/false_positive verdicts, computed for a separate precision study before the correction pass began) rather than a blank annotation guideline read; each correcting subagent was instructed to keep audit-confirmed-correct spans, fix or drop flawed ones, and then do its own fresh full-document read for anything the audit hadn't touched (the audit only judged the model's own predicted spans, not the whole document). Round F is a different labeling mode entirely -- not subagent-labeled at all, but LLM-annotated (Gemini 2.5 Flash / Flash-Lite via litellm, regex-anchored spans resolved locally to character offsets) with no independent human/subagent review pass whatsoever, only the mechanical opf_annotate.py validate check and a per-document span-count sanity filter (docs yielding <4 resolved spans after two annotation attempts were dropped, 4 of 24 candidates: 2 that resolved zero spans across all model/key combinations, 2 more that resolved to a single, likely-spurious span). Treat Round F, and every batch from these rounds' val/test docs, as provisional-quality until they receive the same ensemble verification pass the original seed used, especially before reporting any eval metric that includes them -- Round F in particular has had the least scrutiny of any batch in this corpus.
notes: Seed gold built the subagent way: strict sampling (acordao requires ACORDAO+VOTO+ACORDAM, sentenca requires SENTENCA+dispositivo-formula+operative-verb; despachos excluded), Haiku labeling subagents returning {category,match,nth}, offsets resolved by opf_annotate from-spans, overlaps removed deterministically, then a decorrelated 4-role Sonnet ensemble over val+test. ref_normativa was originally excluded (regex pre-pass at inference) but was added back to the trained label space and bootstrapped into every split via the same regex pre-pass (scripts/ref_normativa_prepass.py) against the already-verified gold text -- see git history for the architecture decision and the regex fix (thousands-separator article numbers, spelled-out inciso/paragrafo/alinea) that preceded it. A second real bug was found and fixed in scripts/ref_normativa_prepass.py's merge_with_opf_spans: it only reliably favored a gold/model span over an overlapping regex span on an exact start-position tie, not on the more common case of a regex match starting earlier but still partially overlapping -- a real gold custas_fim span was being silently dropped by this before the fix. 20-doc JURIS expansion batch added 2026-07-16 (see verification_note above) via the same subagent-labeling + opf_annotate.py from-spans/validate pipeline as the original seed, sourced from src/tjro_juris rather than DJEN cadernos. A follow-up 20-doc Round A batch (also 2026-07-16) closed the preliminar_inicio/fim zero-support gap: candidates were pre-filtered from TJRO JURIS's 2024-08-ACORDAO.parquet for a literal '\\b1\\.\\s*PRELIMINARES?\\b' numbered-heading match (found via manual audit that this heading convention is real but recent -- zero hits in 2005/2008/2017 samples, 21 hits in 2024-08 alone), then subagent-labeled the same way; all 20 confirmed a genuine preliminar section, split 14/3/3 train/val/test (seed 771). A follow-up 20-doc Round B batch (also 2026-07-16) targeted custas_fim/honorarios_fim/fundamentacao_legal: candidates were pre-filtered from TJRO JURIS's 2022-02-SENTENCA.parquet for both 'custas' and 'honorarios' substring mentions (excluding the 10 sentenca ids already used in the earlier expansion batch); several subagents independently anchored custas and honorarios on the exact same fused-clause span (a genuine ambiguity in Juizado Especial boilerplate, not an agent error -- the guideline explicitly allowed it), which opf_annotate validate correctly rejected as BIOES overlaps; 13 such conflicts were resolved deterministically by keeping the first-listed span and dropping the duplicate, then the batch was split 14/3/3 with a hand-picked (not random) val/test doc selection to guarantee each weak category met its per-split minimum despite the tiny (5-20 doc) supply for some categories. An 18-doc Round C batch (also 2026-07-16) pulled a fresh, unfiltered SENTENCA sample from TJRO JURIS's 2020-10-SENTENCA.parquet (a file not used by any prior batch) purely for G5 volume, split 12/3/3 (random, seed 773) -- it produced zero new honorarios_fim, a real finding about how rare that specific closing shape is, not a labeling gap; that finding directly informed Round D's pre-filter design (also 2026-07-16), which specifically excluded the fused 'custas e/ou honorarios' phrasing and targeted homologacao-de-acordo sentencas instead, yielding 7/8 clean honorarios_fim hits and closing the last G2 gap (see per_class_note). A 25-doc Round E batch (2026-07-16) took a different shape from A-D: 25 genuinely novel documents (2017-07-ACORDAO.parquet, a source year never touched by any prior round -- existing gold was all 2020/2022/2024) were run through the extended 10-epoch checkpoint's own inference, independently audited span-by-span by 25 subagents for a precision study (52.9% audited precision, structural pair categories the weakest), then a second wave of 25 correction subagents turned that prediction+audit pair into full corrected gold per document (keep-confirmed / fix-flawed / drop-false-positive / fresh-read-for-the-rest), all acordaos, split 17/4/4 train/val/test (random, seed 2017). Round E deliberately skipped ref_normativa as new labeling effort (see per_class_note) since it was already the most oversupplied category by a wide margin; this also means Round E's per-doc labeling cost was lower than A-D's from-scratch full reads. While reconciling Round E into this manifest, a pre-existing doc_types_total arithmetic bug was also fixed: it previously read acordao:46/sentenca:80 (sum 126) which didn't match the sum of doc_types_per_split (sum 106, matching the true total) -- corrected to acordao:38/sentenca:68 as the pre-Round-E baseline, then Round E's 25 acordaos were added on top. Single-tribunal (TJRO) corpus of 131 docs; G5 volume (needs >=150 total, currently 131) and the waived G4 multi-tribunal gate remain before this gold clears every readiness gate for a real (non --smoke) training run. A 20-doc Round F batch (2026-07-16), prompted by an explicit request to use Gemini for more data, closed G5: 24 sentenca candidates were strict-sampled (same SENTENCA+dispositivo-cue+operative-verb filter as Round C/D, regex-based) from TJRO JURIS's 2023-09-SENTENCA.parquet -- fetched fresh from the Internet Archive item tjro-juris-2023, a source year never touched by any prior round -- then annotated by Gemini (not subagents) via litellm's regex-anchored batch pipeline (scripts/annotate_with_llm.py's approach, reimplemented locally to avoid pulling in that script's unrelated ibis dependency): the model returns a unique-in-document regex pattern with a capturing group per span, which is resolved locally to exact character offsets rather than trusting model-reported offsets directly. This ran into the Gemini free tier's per-key daily request quota (as low as 20 RPD on one of the three rotating keys in GEMINI_API_KEYS, matching the existing quota-avoidance pattern already established in src/causaganha/analysis/llm_analyzer.py, which prefers gemini-2.5-flash-lite at 1000 RPD free over gemini-2.5-flash at 250 RPD and rotates across all available keys on quota/availability errors): the first attempt annotated 12/24 docs before all three keys hit 429/503 on the larger first batch; a rotating retry recovered 10 more (22/24) via flash-lite; two of those had systematically weak regex-anchoring (flash-lite producing non-unique or malformed patterns that opf_annotate's own-document `finditer` count-!=-1 check silently drops), so a targeted fix pass re-ran just those plus the 2 fully-failed docs against gemini-2.5-flash first -- by then all three keys were fully quota-exhausted for flash, so those retries actually landed on the flash-lite fallback, recovering 2 more docs but leaving 2 irrecoverably thin (1 resolved span each) and 2 still at zero; those 2+2 were dropped, leaving 20 clean docs, split 14/3/3 (random, seed 20230916). Round F is the first batch in this corpus with NO subagent or human labeling step of any kind -- see verification_note for why it should be treated as the lowest-confidence batch here despite passing mechanical validation cleanly (0 offset/overlap/label-space errors, 357 spans across 20 docs).
